claim: Anomaly is a domain entity representing a detected statistical anomaly in student emotion data.
AnomalyRepository is a domain repository interface; InMemoryAnomalyRepository (src/infrastructure/storage/) is its implementation.
A dedicated SPEC document exists for InMemoryAnomalyRepository, indicating design-level intent for anomaly persistence.
AnomalyDetectionService is a domain service that detects anomalies in emotion records.
AuditLog is a domain entity recording operation history for audit purposes.
AuditService is an application service that writes audit logs for operations.
Backup is a domain entity representing a snapshot of record data; BackupService and backup/restore API routes exist.
Backup and restore API routes (src/app/api/backup, src/app/api/restore) expose data snapshot operations over HTTP.
NotificationProvider is a domain entity representing an external notification channel; distinct from the UI toast component 'Notification'.
NotificationService is an application service dispatching notifications; settings and history API routes exist under src/app/api/notifications/.
TrendAnalysis is a domain entity for long-term emotion trend analysis; TrendAnalysisService and trends API route exist.
Prisma schema declares only Record and User models; AuditLog, Backup, NotificationProvider, Anomaly, TrendAnalysis have no DB model and persist via in-memory repositories.
Authentication API routes (login/logout/session) exist under src/app/api/auth/ and call the domain AuthenticationService.
AuthorizationService term had layer value 'application', which is outside the allowed layer enum (core|domain|aux) defined by concept-sync v0.3 B-7.
ontology_metrics.json and ontology_budget.yml reported terms_count=43 while ontology.yml actually contains 49 terms; management data had drifted from SOT.
